vision.north_star: Viggo can say only `go`; the agent resolves loose vs repo-local work, repairs the .go contract if needed, then autonomously works toward the defined goal until done, blocked, or budget-exhausted.
vision.wedge: A repo-local autonomous workflow stack: .go holds vision, principles, hierarchy, tasks, evidence, decisions, and loop state; Hermes/Bertus uses it to run a Ralph/old-go-workflow-style build→verify→critic→repair→ship loop without Viggo spamming micro-commands.
vision.target_user: Viggo and future autonomous agents continuing this project.
vision.core_promise: One `go` can turn rough intent into a valid .go contract, split the goal into tasks, claim/execute/recheck/devil/repair/commit/finish each task, self-reflect, capture lessons, and report compactly.
non_goals: no random feature invention from autonomy
no broad scope expansion without explicit goal fit
no command-spam handoff back to Viggo
success_metrics: a bare `go` routes correctly between loose work and repo-local .go work
valid .go contract is repaired before execution
open work is split into executable tasks with acceptance and verification
loop continues across tasks without Viggo re-triggering each phase
recheck/devil/self-reflect findings create repairs or follow-up tasks before final done
final report includes commits, verification, and open/blocker state

planned_direction.target: Zelfstandig releasbare Go-taken met expliciete model/effortkeuze en hervatbare contextoverdracht; done vereist de afgesproken geverifieerde release.
success_metrics: A: iedere nieuwe releaseplichtige taak heeft gekoppeld bewijs voor checks, review, commit/push, publicatie en eventuele livecontrole.
B: twee opeenvolgende taken gebruiken aantoonbaar verschillende gekozen model/effortprofielen zonder stille terugval.
C: een verse worker hervat een onderbroken actieve taak met actuele code-, fase- en bewijscontext zonder chatgeschiedenis.
Verse templateclones erven de gevalideerde contracten zonder onderhoudsbacklog of fictieve historische releasebewijzen.
Een taak behoudt één gecontroleerde branch/worktree bij modelwissels en herstel; alleen de definitieve geïntegreerde revisie met geldig fase- en releasebewijs kan done worden.
planned_direction.completion_note: Thirteen ABC tasks completed. Opt-in product lifecycle, explicit task/critic models, durable context, primary controller with owned worktrees and serial verified release. Fresh phase workers supported; persistent-session/subagent adapters remain deferred.

proposed_directions.target: Go bestuurt één projectrun met parallelle geïsoleerde workers, duurzame coördinatie en een volledige geverifieerde lifecycle per taak.
success_metrics: Twee onafhankelijke builds overlappen aantoonbaar; scope/resourceconflicten worden tegengehouden.
Na een gewijzigde main krijgt de volgende kandidaat nieuw definitief bewijs en een eigen release.
Controlleruitval veroorzaakt geen dubbele writers, verloren taakvoortgang of dubbele publicatie.
non_goals: Multi-host of nested teams in v1
Vervangen van bestaande taak- en releasebewijzen door chats
proposed_directions.note: Ontwerp op verzoek van 2026-09-18; eerdere completed ABC-direction en actuele runtimecontracten blijven ongewijzigd.

proposed_directions.target: Eén begrensde seriële Go-run onderzoekt de opdracht, toetst visie/architectuur, maakt uitvoerbare taken, bouwt/herstelt en levert elke zelfstandige taak geverifieerd op zonder herhaalde gebruikersstarts.
success_metrics: Iedere oorspronkelijke uitkomst heeft taak-, besluit-, bewijs- en releaseherkomst; geen betekenisverlies tussen verkenning en oplevering.
Meerdere taken worden autonoom afgehandeld, met begrensd herstel en cumulatief budget na onderbreking.
Lege taakvoorraad of aanwezige succescriteria worden niet gelijkgesteld aan bereikt productdoel.
Een echte nachtrun rapporteert gemeten duur, menselijke interventies, actuele Git-state en geverifieerde live uitkomsten.

principles.statement: Every autonomous go run must define or repair the end goal, acceptance, verification, and task boundary before implementation.

principles.statement: A task is not done at first passing verification; recheck/devil/critic and repair/self-reflect must run for non-trivial work.

principles.statement: The go loop defaults to solo or lead-plus-one-worker; parallel builders require disjoint modify scopes and a reviewer lane, while overlapping modify scopes remain serial.

data.title: Expliciete modelkeuze zonder stille fallback
data.context: User selected Astra High and authorized the ABC execution sequence; installed Codex model/list capabilities inspected.
data.decision: Freeze explicit task and optional critic selections at first execution. Query the installed Codex catalog before any worker writes; force runtime model and reasoning options. Introduce no implicit global model or automatic escalation. Keep effective identity unconfirmed unless authoritative runtime evidence exists. Hermes/custom controlled selection is unsupported until its adapter explicitly implements it; legacy commands remain usable.
consequences: No model quality/cost rankings or provider guarantees are inferred from a catalog response.

data.title: Eén expliciete taakwerkplek met canonieke control state
data.context: User authorized the prepared ABC/legacy execution sequence; one worktree per task and serial integration were the planned baseline.
data.decision: Require explicit workspace path, branch and base branch/commit. Bind registry and Git worktree marker to task/owner/run; resolve registered-worktree Go commands to canonical .go. Use existing process locks for creation, writing and serial integration. Refuse foreign paths, scope violations and unproven cleanup. No implicit branch heuristic, publisher, service-port or database policy.
consequences: Active-task orchestration and handoff consume these primitives in abc-03/04; cleanup never republishes.

data.title: Durable worker context verified against current state
data.context: abc-03 follows shipped task/model/workspace contracts; workers must continue without chat history.
data.decision: Create immutable per-dispatch snapshots in canonical .go with file/hash references and explicit phase feedback. Verify task, workspace, Git/index/worktree content and raw evidence before launch. Keep legacy inline environment behavior; opted-in tasks use bounded references and explicitly selected repo-local context.
consequences: Active resume and model topology remain abc-04/09; raw evidence and code remain authoritative.

data.title: Exclusive managed phase resume with explicit initial workspace
data.context: abc-04 follows verified model selection, owned workspaces and durable phase context; current loop cannot resume after a build exhausts its budget.
data.decision: Add an opt-in managed native phase runner with explicit initial workspace bindings, persisted phase/effect intent and completion, preserved model/context/requirements, and process-aware exclusive recovery. Resume from proven phase; invalidate affected proof after drift. Support explicit stopped-owner local relocation; do not infer cross-host quiescence or old checkpoint phases.
consequences: Release/deployment publishers remain abc-05/06/07; the managed runner exposes their intent/readback and cleanup recovery boundaries.

data.title: Require content-bound proof before opted-in completion
data.context: User GO authorizes abc-05 after v0.3.19; old finish-before-ship and prose-only evidence remain insufficient for self-contained product tasks.
data.decision: Apply one strict completion gate to current opted-in finish, approval and reporting. Capture declared local checks plus review and content identity, verify explicit Git-tag/GitHub-release readback, and keep unknown or failed shipping pending. Preserve historical done records/unconfigured legacy semantics under abc-d01; publisher/deploy automation follows in abc-06/07.
consequences: Read-only release verification is distinct from publication authority; no model-success or populated field can replace command and remote proof.

data.title: Publish configured task releases through durable intent and exact readback
data.context: User GO continues after abc-05 v0.3.21. Completion proof is enforced; the managed runner still stops at release_pending.
data.decision: Add an explicitly configured controller publisher for version preparation, final proof, scoped commit/integration, annotated tag and GitHub release. Bind task/run/owner, frozen profile and explicit push authority. Serialize publication, reconcile every interrupted effect by exact readback, reject stale bases/conflicting tags, and finish through the shared gate. Keep deployment and default migration in their existing later tasks.
consequences: Unconfigured profiles do not gain publication rights. Inconclusive remote results remain pending; owned workspaces and evidence survive retries. No GitHub Actions or silent force operations.

data.title: Require explicit target authority and authoritative live deployment proof
data.context: User GO continues after abc-06 v0.3.22 publication. Package/deployment providers remain project-specific onboarding inputs.
data.decision: Extend explicit release profiles with no-deployment policy or controlled package/deploy/readback argv adapters. Freeze target and separate deployment authorization; bind released commit/version and optional artifact hash. Require stable idempotency identity and authoritative absent/accepted/live/unknown observations. Retain pending state on inconclusive results and finish only through verified live proof. Use local fixtures and no real production target in this implementation.
consequences: Existing profiles remain release-only. New required deployments cannot use Git push permission as deployment authority. No automatic rollback, production data changes, GitHub Actions or provider selection.

data.title: Adopt lifecycle policy explicitly with recoverable state and preserved provenance
data.context: User GO continues after abc-07 v0.3.23. Existing project history and user-selected policies must remain distinguishable from new opt-in defaults.
data.decision: Add an explicit lifecycle configuration path to repository migration, separate from stack-pin/schema updates. Preview before apply, journal exact state for recovery/rollback, convert only eligible open records and preserve existing overrides/history. Reuse intake resolution and preserve full task/project contract provenance in non-executable review bundles.
consequences: No inferred model or shipping/deployment authority, no historic proof fabrication, no active-run transfer, no mandatory broad skill chain and no global skill mutations.

data.title: Verse workers met repositorygebonden context als basis
data.context: User GO; shipped owned workspace/context/resume baseline and locally inspected Codex 0.153.4 protocol. abc-09 will capture reproducible fixture proof; live baseline proof remains abc-10.
data.decision: Support fresh ephemeral native CLI workers at task/phase boundaries with frozen per-phase profiles, canonical context snapshots and one owned worktree. Defer persistent app-server turn/session adapters and subagent adapters: protocol capability exists but Go-specific ownership, recovery and attribution integration is not implemented. No mid-turn switch or implicit new worktree per model.
consequences: Deferred alternatives do not block the baseline. Any later adapter must prove exact session identity, explicit per-phase overrides, canonical recovery, exclusive writer and read-only critic. No chat transcript is the lifecycle source of truth.

data.title: Reuse explicit decision dependencies and content review for task readiness
data.context: Authorized task asks for minimum compatible readiness improvement. Audit found architecture claim returns early for none/local tasks before inspecting explicit governing references. Structural checks and process success do not judge semantic adequacy.
data.decision: Honor explicitly declared architecture scope/decision dependencies even at none/local impact, without requiring new metadata or conformance on unreferenced simple tasks. Retain existing material/foundational requirements. Strengthen repo-local authoring and native build/critic guidance with a source-grounded review disposition and matching requirement evidence. No new readiness boolean, keyword classifier, global skill change or approval system.
consequences: Unreferenced none/local tasks and legacy history remain unchanged; explicitly missing, draft or non-accepted governing dependencies prevent dependent claim and finish.
Research may examine unresolved choices within research-only scope; it must not declare the unresolved proposed rule as an accepted implementation prerequisite.
Routine delegated tuning stays autonomous. Unsupported bug-fix or requested-outcome claims remain pending/blocked through existing outcome and critic paths.

briefs.title: Architecture lane governance contract
outcomes: Consequential work cannot complete without traceability to an accepted governing architecture decision.

in: Architecture classification, claim preflight and finish conformance behavior
out: Mandating a newly authored ADR for every implementation task
boundaries: Task metadata, scoped briefs, decision ledger and architecture event stream

decision_rights: accept or revise governing architecture decisions and risks
propose options and verify conformance without claiming human authority

constraints: The existing .go/decisions/events.jsonl ledger remains the only decision source of truth.
Legacy repositories and none/local tasks remain backward compatible.
A task may reuse an existing accepted governing decision; the gate must not force duplicate ADRs.

quality_attributes.scenario: A task is effectively classified as material or foundational and reaches claim or finish preflight.
quality_attributes.measure: Material or foundational tasks with zero exact accepted governing decision references

risks: An overly literal gate could incentivize meaningless ADR creation instead of reuse of a real governing decision.

data.title: Require accepted governing decisions for consequential tasks
data.context: The released architecture lane can currently claim and finish material work when a brief defines quality attributes but neither the task nor its applicable briefs reference any decision. Viggo explicitly authorized closing this gap with Go after reviewing the trade-off.
data.decision: Every effectively material or foundational task must resolve at least one exact accepted governing decision from its task metadata or applicable accepted briefs. Reusing an existing governing decision is preferred; a new per-task ADR is not required when an accepted decision already governs the work.
consequences: Claim fails with an actionable missing-governing-decision finding when the combined reference set is empty.
Existing missing or non-accepted referenced decisions continue to fail closed.
None/local tasks and legacy repositories remain unaffected.

quality_attributes.scenario: A task is effectively classified as material or foundational and reaches claim or finish preflight.
quality_attributes.measure: Material or foundational tasks with zero exact accepted governing decision references

task_design_review.evidence_required: Concrete reasons and inspected source/evidence references in existing task/run review evidence.
task_design_review.author: Before implementation, assess task design from the actual task, referenced decisions and evidence. For substantial work, identify observable before/after behavior, relevant states/transitions and edge cases, boundaries/non-goals, dependencies and matching proof. Distinguish accepted rules, proposals, bounded delegated tuning and unresolved material choices with their owner and resolution gate. Record ready, design_research_first or blocked_on_material_decision with concrete reasons and source/evidence references in the existing task/run review evidence; the label alone proves nothing. A schema-valid task, keyword match or long description does not establish semantic readiness. Use existing architecture decision references and opted-in execution dependencies for real prerequisites; do not hide blocking dependencies in prose. Research-only work can resolve open choices within its own scope; do not implement the dependent behavior or silently change a fix request into research completion. Routine reversible tuning remains delegated within stated bounds; a trivial fix needs only proportionate behavior and verification, not a new ADR or user approval. If a material implementation choice is unresolved, report the blocker and research/decision needed before product edits; do not invent the answer.
task_design_review.critic: Review semantic adequacy against the original requested outcomes, not just schema validity or successful processes. Inspect the behavior, relevant state/edge cases, accepted rules, delegated bounds and actual evidence. Explain blocking gaps with source references and name which R# remains unproven. An unknown root cause or unreproduced reported bug is not a verified fix; a hypothesis or preparation document does not satisfy a requested behavior correction. Leave those outcomes pending/blocked through the existing result protocol rather than declaring success. Research can succeed on research evidence only when that is the authorized task outcome. Use relevant runtime, visual, motion or listening evidence and references when the change needs them; do not demand irrelevant media or a new approval for bounded tuning. Content judgment belongs to the reviewer and must include reasons and inspected evidence; a readiness label or unverified self-attestation is insufficient.
